questions.title: Influenza causes fever by raising the hypothalamic set point
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: How does an influenza viral infection typically cause the onset of a fever in a patient?

options.A: Complete failure of the sweat glands
options.B: The hypothalamic set point is raised
options.D: Peripheral cold receptors are intensely activated

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sweat gland failure is not the mechanism by which influenza produces fever; the driving event is upstream, at the level of the hypothalamic set point itself.
explanations.B: Correct. Cytokines released during the immune response to influenza act as endogenous pyrogens on the hypothalamus, raising its thermoregulatory set point; the body then generates and conserves heat until core temperature reaches this new, higher target. This is the same set-point-elevation mechanism behind any infectious fever, not something unique to influenza.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Heat production increases, not decreases, during the rising phase of fever, as shivering thermogenesis is recruited to reach the elevated set point.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Peripheral cold receptor activation is not the mechanism; the hypothalamus behaves as though the body is cold because the set point itself has moved, not because peripheral cold sensing has intensified.

questions.learning_objective: Explain fever as pyrogen-mediated resetting of the hypothalamic set point upward, and state that the ensuing shivering and vasoconstriction are the normal response to a body temperature that is now below the new set point.
